title: Year 7 Maths summary and memory tips

scenes.heading: Year 7 Maths summary and memory tips
scenes.sub: A whole year of maths in two minutes
scenes.say: A whole year of maths in two minutes? Let's do it. Here are the big rules from Year 7, and the memory tricks that make them stick.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Packing a school bag: only what you need for tomorrow
scenes.science: Revising: the key rules and tricks, not every page
scenes.breaks: A bag can leave things at home. In a test you might need any rule, so go back to the lessons for anything shaky.
scenes.say: Think of revision like packing your school bag the night before. You don't take every book, just what you need. This summary packs the key rules and best memory tricks. If a chapter feels shaky, go back to its lessons.

scenes.heading: Number
points: BIDMAS: ×, ÷ left to right, then +, − left to right
HCF: share into groups. LCM: next time together
1 is not prime; 2 is the only even prime
scenes.say: Number first. BIDMAS: brackets, indices, then multiply and divide left to right, then add and subtract left to right. So four plus five times three squared is forty-nine. HCF is for sharing into equal groups; LCM is for the next time things happen together. One is not prime, and two is the only even prime.
scenes.caption: Number first. BIDMAS: brackets, indices, then × and ÷ left to right, then + and − left to right. So 4 + 5 × 3² = 49. HCF: share into equal groups. LCM: next time together. 1 is not prime, and 2 is the only even prime.

scenes.heading: Fractions and decimals
steps: Add decimals: line up the points
scenes.say: Fractions and decimals. To add fractions, make the bottoms the same, then add the tops. To divide, keep, change, flip. Of means times, so half of ten is a half times ten. And to add decimals, line up the points.
scenes.caption: To add fractions, make the bottoms the same, then add the tops. To divide: Keep, Change, Flip. "Of" means times: half of 10 is ½ × 10. To add decimals, line up the points.

scenes.heading: Negative numbers
scenes.say: Negative numbers. Same signs smile, different signs frown. Negative three times negative four is twelve. Negative twenty divided by four is negative five. Two signs side by side work the same way: five minus negative four is five plus four, which is nine.
scenes.caption: Same signs smile, different signs frown. (−3) × (−4) = 12. −20 ÷ 4 = −5. Two signs side by side work the same way: 5 − (−4) = 5 + 4 = 9.

scenes.heading: Algebra and equations
scenes.question: Solve 4x + 7 = 35.
scenes.say: Solve four x plus seven equals thirty-five. Socks and shoes: undo the last step first. Subtract seven from both sides: four x equals twenty-eight. Divide both sides by four: x equals seven. Check: four times seven plus seven is thirty-five.
scenes.caption: Solve 4x + 7 = 35. Socks and shoes: undo the last step first. Subtract 7 from both sides: 4x = 28. Divide both sides by 4: x = 7. Check: 4 × 7 + 7 = 35 ✓

scenes.heading: Shapes and measurement
notes: Perimeter cm, area cm², volume cm³
scenes.say: Shapes. Half a pizza is one hundred and eighty degrees: a straight line, or the angles in a triangle. A whole pizza is three hundred and sixty: a full turn, or a quadrilateral. Perimeter is in centimetres, area in square centimetres, volume in cubic centimetres.
scenes.caption: Half a pizza is 180°: a straight line, or the angles in a triangle. A whole pizza is 360°: a full turn, or a quadrilateral. Perimeter in cm, area in cm², volume in cm³.

scenes.heading: Data, chance and algorithms
points: Mean: add and divide. Median: the middle
Mode: most common. Range: biggest − smallest
scenes.say: Data and chance. Hey diddle diddle, the median's the middle; you add and divide for the mean. The mode appears the most; the range is biggest take away smallest. Probability is favourable over total. And in a flowchart, diamonds decide.
scenes.caption: Hey diddle diddle, the median's the middle; you add and divide for the mean. The mode appears the most; the range is biggest − smallest. Probability = favourable ÷ total. In a flowchart, diamonds decide.

points: BIDMAS: left to right for partners
Do the same to both sides
180° in a triangle, 360° in a quad
scenes.say: Quick recap. BIDMAS, partners left to right. Same bottoms, add the tops. Same signs smile, different signs frown. Do the same to both sides. One eighty in a triangle, three sixty in a quadrilateral. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. BIDMAS, partners left to right. Same bottoms, add the tops. Same signs smile, different signs frown. Do the same to both sides. 180° in a triangle, 360° in a quadrilateral. Now try the practice questions!
